For x=y=0 the root is sqrt(0)=0, so there is no div, arccos or signTest. This directly refutes every-call-exactly-one arccos. Over reals the squared norm is nonnegative and its square root vanishes exactly for x=y=0; no exotic negative-squared-norm path is needed.
substantive_reconstruction.nonzero_nonnegative_y_path: After the initial three fields, one sqrt and one comparison, the else branch executes div(x,r) (one field), arccos (one angle), and signTest(y) (one comparison). For y>=0 the signed value is pure(a), zero additional cost. mul(2,signed) and sub(0,doubled) add two fields. Total is (6,1,1,2); trig/read/write/emit remain zero. Input (1,0) has r=1 and y<0 false, so realizes this trace even though arccos(1)=0 and the resulting double/negation values vanish. Operations are charged by calls, not canceled by algebraic simplification.
substantive_reconstruction.negative_y_path: For y<0, which already forces the real norm nonzero, the same nonzero path additionally executes sub(0,a), one field operation. Thus total is (7,1,1,2), with other counters zero. Input (0,-1) has r=1 and a=arccos(0), so realizes it. There is exactly one arccos on either nonzero path; only the negative-y path attains all components of the full budget jointly.
